headline: Models infer unmeasured molecular layers from co-measured omics, from spatial protein to RNA-ATAC
label: Cross Modal Molecular Layer Inference
summary: Preprints this week predict protein, chromatin-linked and isoform layers from measured RNA, with oncology models handling survival and drug response.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring an unmeasured molecular layer from a measured one. TSNR predicts spatial protein abundance from spatial transcriptomics using protein-specific center signals plus compact broad molecular context under a Huber loss. MUTUAL aligns frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings into a shared RNA-ATAC latent space trained on 3.0M multiome cells. IsoPrism allocates isoform proportions from short-read single-cell and spatial transcriptomes, and Top2All benchmarks Geneformer-based reconstruction of transcriptome-wide expression from sparse high-expression genes in mouse adrenal RNA-seq. A secondary oncology strand is less directly cross-modal: CMVAE, GOTSurv, DMG-PoE (handling modality incompleteness), HHRM and MODAE+ address survival, stratification, subtyping and cell-line-to-tumour drug-response transfer. The newer emphasis is reuse of foundation-model embeddings and structure-aware priors for cross-layer prediction.
